revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Snack Bags
revealWordProblem.text:
Andrew has four types of nuts and a different quantity of each type, shown on the bags. He wants to make 4 snack bags of each type of nut, and he will not mix the nuts together in a bag.
Question: What will be the weight of the snack bags for each type of nut? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Four bags of nuts labeled with their weights: almonds one-half pound, cashews one-fourth pound, peanuts two-fifths pound, walnuts three-fourths pound.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Each amount is being shared equally among 4 bags, so divide each weight by 4. Almonds: ½ ÷ 4 = ⅛ pound per bag. Cashews: ¼ ÷ 4 = 1/16 pound per bag. Peanuts: ⅖ ÷ 4 = 1/10 pound per bag. Walnuts: ¾ ÷ 4 = 3/16 pound per bag. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by ¼, which is why every answer is smaller than the amount Andrew started with.

questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3. To find that, put a 1 under the 3 and use Keep, Change, Flip: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
choiceFeedback: That's multiplication (3 × 1/4). Division asks 'how many' pieces, not 'groups of' pieces.
Subtraction is not division. Division by a fraction asks 'how many pieces fit.'
That's finding a part of the whole. Division by a fraction asks 'how many of this size fit inside.'
hints: Re-read the expression: 3 is the total amount and 1/4 is the size of one piece. What question could that setup be asking?
Dividing by a fraction asks a counting question about pieces, not 'a part of.' Predict: should the result be bigger or smaller than 3?
Picture a 3-foot tape cut into 1/4-foot pieces, then set it up: put a 1 under the 3 and flip the 1/4.
questions.explanationEs: 3 ÷ 1/4 pregunta cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/4 caben en 3. Para hallarlo, pon un 1 debajo del 3 y usa Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
choicesEs: Cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben en 3
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la expresión: 3 es la cantidad total y 1/4 es el tamaño de una pieza. ¿Qué pregunta podría estar haciendo ese planteamiento?
Dividir entre una fracción hace una pregunta de conteo sobre piezas, no de 'una parte de'. Predice: ¿el resultado debe ser mayor o menor que 3?
Imagina una cinta de 3 pies cortada en piezas de 1/4 de pie y luego plantéalo: pon un 1 debajo del 3 y voltea el 1/4.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
questions.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is written 2 ÷ 1/3. Put a 1 under the 2, then Keep, Change, Flip: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies instead of divides. To find how many pieces fit, we divide by the piece size.
You flipped the order. The whole (2) goes first; the piece size (1/3) is the divisor.
Addition combines amounts. To find how many pieces fit, we divide.
hints: Find the two jobs: which number is the total being split, and which is the size of each piece?
Division setups read total ÷ piece size. The total always sits in front of the ÷ sign.
Here the total is 2 and each piece is 1/3. Build the expression with the total first, then check it against each choice.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión significa "cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 hay en 2"?
questions.explanationEs: Encontrar cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 caben en 2 se escribe 2 ÷ 1/3. Pon un 1 debajo del 2 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
hintsEs: Encuentra los dos papeles: ¿cuál número es el total que se reparte y cuál es el tamaño de cada pieza?
Los planteamientos de división se leen total ÷ tamaño de la pieza. El total siempre va delante del signo ÷.
Aquí el total es 2 y cada pieza es 1/3. Arma la expresión con el total primero y luego compárala con cada opción.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: Write 4 ÷ 1/2. Put a 1 under the 4, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 pieces.
choiceFeedback: You divided 4 by 2. Dividing by 1/2 means flipping it: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8.
Dividing by 1/2 makes the answer bigger. Flipping 1/2 gives 2/1, a factor larger than 1.
You did not flip the divisor. Put a 1 under the 4, flip 1/2 to 2/1, then multiply.
hints: Note the numbers: the rope is 4 feet long, and every piece is 1/2 foot — smaller than a whole foot.
Start small: figure out how many 1/2-foot pieces fit into just 1 foot of rope.
Put a 1 under the 4 to get 4/1, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1.
questions.stemEs: Una cuerda mide 4 pies de largo. ¿Cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie se pueden cortar de ella?
questions.explanationEs: Escribe 4 ÷ 1/2. Pon un 1 debajo del 4 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 piezas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en los números: la cuerda mide 4 pies y cada pieza mide 1/2 pie, menos que un pie entero.
Empieza en pequeño: averigua cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie caben en solo 1 pie de cuerda.
Pon un 1 debajo del 4 para obtener 4/1 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1.

steps: 1. Put a 1 under the whole number so it is a fraction
2. Keep, Change, Flip — keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the second
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Interpret Division of Fractions is assuming that dividing always makes the answer smaller. For 4 ÷ 1/3, students reason 'dividing shrinks the number' and compute 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.3 instead of asking how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 4 feet (each whole foot holds 3 thirds, so 4 × 3 = 12). Before you submit, check: if the divisor is a fraction smaller than 1, the quotient must be BIGGER than the dividend, not smaller.

level1.stem: A half-pan of brownies is shared equally among 4 people. How much of the whole pan does each get?
level1.explanation: This is 1/2 ÷ 4. The whole number is second this time, so put a 1 under the 4, then Keep, Change, Flip: 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8 of the whole pan.
choiceFeedback: That divides 4 by 1/2 — the opposite question.
That flips the problem into a multiplication of the wrong pair.
That gives the whole half to one person instead of sharing it.
hints: Draw half a pan, then split that half into 4 equal parts.
How many of those parts fit in the WHOLE pan?
The whole number is second here. Put a 1 under the 4 to get 4/1, then flip it to 1/4 and multiply.
level1.stemEs: Medio molde de brownies se reparte en partes iguales entre 4 personas. ¿Cuánto del molde entero recibe cada una?
level1.explanationEs: Esto es 1/2 ÷ 4. Esta vez el número entero va segundo, así que pon un 1 debajo del 4 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8 del molde entero.
hintsEs: Dibuja medio molde y luego divide esa mitad en 4 partes iguales.
¿Cuántas de esas partes caben en TODO el molde?
Aquí el número entero va segundo. Pon un 1 debajo del 4 para obtener 4/1, luego voltéalo a 1/4 y multiplica.

level1.explanation: Put a 1 under the 6: 6/1 ÷ 1/5. Keep, Change, Flip gives 6/1 × 5/1 = 30.
choiceFeedback: You multiplied by 1/5 instead of flipping it. Keep, Change, Flip gives 6/1 × 5/1 = 30.
You flipped the wrong number. Flip only the divisor: 6/1 × 5/1 = 30.
Flipping a fraction smaller than 1 gives a factor larger than 1, so the answer grows past 6.
hints: 6 ÷ 1/5 asks: how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6 wholes? Predict first — more or fewer than 6?
Find how many fifths make 1 whole, then use that count for all 6 wholes.
Put a 1 under the 6, flip 1/5 to 5/1, then multiply across.
level1.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del 6: 6/1 ÷ 1/5. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea da 6/1 × 5/1 = 30.
hintsEs: 6 ÷ 1/5 pregunta: ¿cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/5 caben en 6 enteros? Predice primero: ¿más o menos de 6?
Averigua cuántos quintos forman 1 entero y luego usa esa cantidad para los 6 enteros.
Pon un 1 debajo del 6, voltea 1/5 a 5/1 y luego multiplica en línea.

level2.stem: A shelf is 5 feet long. Books are each 1/4 foot wide. How many books fit on the shelf? Which expression represents this?
level2.explanation: The expression is 5 ÷ 1/4. Put a 1 under the 5, then Keep, Change, Flip: 5/1 × 4/1 = 20 books.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies instead of dividing. To count pieces that fit, divide the whole by the piece size.
You flipped the division. The shelf length (5) is the dividend; the book width (1/4) is the divisor.
Addition combines lengths. To find how many books fit, divide the shelf length by one book's width.
hints: Spot the roles: 5 feet is the whole shelf, and 1/4 foot is the width of one book.
Counting how many books fit means total ÷ piece size — and the count should be bigger than 5, since books are thin.
Set it up as 5 ÷ 1/4, put a 1 under the 5, and flip the divisor to test which choice matches.
level2.stemEs: Un estante mide 5 pies de largo. Cada libro tiene 1/4 de pie de ancho. ¿Cuántos libros caben en el estante? ¿Qué expresión representa esto?
level2.explanationEs: La expresión es 5 ÷ 1/4. Pon un 1 debajo del 5 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 5/1 × 4/1 = 20 libros.
hintsEs: Identifica los papeles: 5 pies es el estante completo y 1/4 de pie es el ancho de un libro.
Contar cuántos libros caben significa total ÷ tamaño de la pieza, y el conteo debe ser mayor que 5 porque los libros son delgados.
Plantéalo como 5 ÷ 1/4, pon un 1 debajo del 5 y voltea el divisor para probar qué opción coincide.

level2.explanation: 6 ÷ 1/5 means how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 6 × 5 = 30.
choiceFeedback: You multiplied 6 by 1/5 instead of dividing by 1/5. Dividing by a small fraction gives a much bigger answer.
You flipped it backward. Try: each whole has 5 fifths, so 6 wholes have 6 × 5 = 30 fifths.
Dividing by a fraction smaller than 1 gives an answer bigger than you started with, not 1.
hints: 6 ÷ 1/5 asks: how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6 wholes? Predict first — more or fewer than 6?
Find how many fifths make 1 whole, then use that count for all 6 wholes.
One whole holds 5 fifths. With 6 wholes, count 5 fifths for each whole — set up that multiplication.
level2.explanationEs: 6 ÷ 1/5 significa cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/5 caben en 6. Cada entero tiene 5 quintos, así que 6 × 5 = 30.
hintsEs: 6 ÷ 1/5 pregunta: ¿cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/5 caben en 6 enteros? Predice primero: ¿más o menos de 6?
Averigua cuántos quintos forman 1 entero y luego usa esa cantidad para los 6 enteros.
Un entero tiene 5 quintos. Con 6 enteros, cuenta 5 quintos por cada entero y plantea esa multiplicación.

level2.stem: Agent Cole has 8 feet of evidence rope and cuts it into 1/3-foot pieces for tagging. What does 8 ÷ 1/3 mean?
choices: How many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet
8 feet shortened by 1/3 of a foot
8 pieces that are each 1/3 foot long
level2.explanation: Dividing by 1/3 asks how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet. Each foot holds 3 thirds, so 8 × 3 = 24 pieces.
choiceFeedback: You're thinking of multiplication. Does dividing by 1/3 ask 'how many parts' or 'what is part of the whole'?
Subtracting doesn't match the problem. Division by fractions asks 'how many pieces fit.'
That's describing the pieces, not what 8 ÷ 1/3 means. What question does the division ask?
level2.stemEs: El agente Cole tiene 8 pies de cuerda de evidencia y la corta en piezas de 1/3 de pie para etiquetarlas. ¿Qué significa 8 ÷ 1/3?
level2.explanationEs: Dividir entre 1/3 pregunta cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en 8 pies. Cada pie contiene 3 tercios, así que 8 × 3 = 24 piezas.
hints: Dividing by a fraction always asks the same question: how many pieces of that size fit inside the whole amount?
Name the two parts of the problem first — the whole amount of rope and the length of one piece. The whole amount comes first in the division.
Here the whole amount is 8 feet and each piece is 1/3 foot. Picture a single foot of rope: how many 1/3-foot pieces does one foot hold? Then extend that thinking to all 8 feet.
hintsEs: Dividir entre una fracción siempre hace la misma pregunta: ¿cuántas piezas de ese tamaño caben dentro de la cantidad total?
Primero nombra las dos partes del problema: la cantidad total de cuerda y el largo de una pieza. La cantidad total va primero en la división.
Aquí la cantidad total es 8 pies y cada pieza mide 1/3 de pie. Imagina un solo pie de cuerda: ¿cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en un pie? Luego extiende esa idea a los 8 pies.
choicesEs: Cuántas piezas de 1/3 de pie caben en 8 pies
8 piezas que miden 1/3 de pie cada una

level2.stem: Picture clue: a 5-inch fingerprint strip is split into 1/6-inch slivers under the microscope. Which division does the picture show, and what is the count?
level2.explanation: How many 1/6-inch slivers fit into 5 inches? Each inch holds 6 sixths, so 5 × 6 = 30 slivers.
choiceFeedback: You switched the numbers. Is the 5 the whole being split, or the size of each piece?
You flipped the division. The whole (5) should be first, and the piece size (1/6) should be second.
That's multiplication, not division. Count how many pieces fit, not the area they cover.
level2.stemEs: Pista visual: una tira de huella digital de 5 pulgadas se divide en tiritas de 1/6 de pulgada bajo el microscopio. ¿Qué división muestra la imagen y cuál es el conteo?
level2.explanationEs: ¿Cuántas tiritas de 1/6 de pulgada caben en 5 pulgadas? Cada pulgada contiene 6 sextos, así que 5 × 6 = 30 tiritas.
hints: The picture shows one long strip being cut into many small equal pieces, which is a division situation.
Write the whole length first, then divide by the size of one sliver. Cutting into smaller pieces makes the count larger than the length.
A single inch splits into 6 sixths. Use that to reason about how the count grows across all 5 inches.
hintsEs: La imagen muestra una tira larga cortada en muchas piezas iguales y pequeñas, lo cual es una situación de división.
Escribe primero el largo total y luego divide entre el tamaño de una tirita. Cortar en piezas más pequeñas hace que el conteo sea mayor que el largo.
Una sola pulgada se divide en 6 sextos. Usa eso para razonar cómo crece el conteo a lo largo de las 5 pulgadas.

level2.prompt: Dividing 6 by 1/2 gives 12, but dividing 6 by 2 gives 3. How can dividing by a smaller number (1/2) give a bigger answer than dividing by a larger number (2)? Explain using a real-world example.
level2.sentenceFrame: When I divide 6 by 2, I am ___. When I divide 6 by 1/2, I am ___. The answer is bigger because ___.
level2.hint: Compare the two divisions: what question does each one ask? Use 'fit into' and 'share' in your thinking.
hints: Re-read both: 6 ÷ 2 splits 6 into 2 equal groups, but 6 ÷ 1/2 counts how many half-size pieces fit into 6.
Pick a real object — 6 sandwiches shared between 2 people versus 6 sandwiches cut into halves — and describe both.
Start your answer with the sharing story (6 split into 2 groups), then explain what cutting into halves does to the count.
level2.explanation: The two expressions ask different questions. 6 ÷ 2 shares 6 into 2 equal groups, so each group gets 3. 6 ÷ 1/2 counts how many half-size pieces fit inside 6, and since each whole holds 2 halves, there are 12. Smaller pieces means a bigger count, so dividing by 1/2 gives a larger quotient than dividing by 2.
level2.explanationEs: Las dos expresiones hacen preguntas distintas. 6 ÷ 2 reparte 6 en 2 grupos iguales, así que a cada grupo le tocan 3. 6 ÷ 1/2 cuenta cuántas piezas de medio caben dentro de 6 y, como cada entero contiene 2 mitades, hay 12. Piezas más pequeñas significan una cuenta más grande, así que dividir entre 1/2 da un cociente mayor que dividir entre 2.
level2.promptEs: Dividir 6 entre 1/2 da 12, pero dividir 6 entre 2 da 3. ¿Cómo puede dividir entre un número más pequeño (1/2) dar una respuesta más grande que dividir entre un número más grande (2)? Explica con un ejemplo de la vida real.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer ambas: 6 ÷ 2 reparte 6 en 2 grupos iguales, pero 6 ÷ 1/2 cuenta cuántas piezas de medio tamaño caben en 6.
Escoge un objeto real —6 sándwiches repartidos entre 2 personas frente a 6 sándwiches cortados por la mitad— y describe las dos situaciones.
Empieza tu respuesta con la historia de repartir (6 en 2 grupos) y luego explica qué le hace al conteo cortar por la mitad.

level3.prompt: Dividing 6 by 1/2 gives 12, but dividing 6 by 2 gives 3. How can dividing by a smaller number (1/2) give a bigger answer than dividing by a larger number (2)? Explain using a real-world example.
level3.sentenceFrame: When I divide 6 by 2, I am ___. When I divide 6 by 1/2, I am ___. The answer is bigger because ___.
level3.hint: Compare the two divisions: what question does each one ask? Use 'fit into' and 'share' in your thinking.
hints: Re-read both: 6 ÷ 2 splits 6 into 2 equal groups, but 6 ÷ 1/2 counts how many half-size pieces fit into 6.
Pick a real object — 6 sandwiches shared between 2 people versus 6 sandwiches cut into halves — and describe both.
Start your answer with the sharing story (6 split into 2 groups), then explain what cutting into halves does to the count.
level3.explanation: The two expressions ask different questions, and the flip shows why. 6 ÷ 2 is 6/1 × 1/2 = 3, because flipping 2/1 gives a factor smaller than 1. 6 ÷ 1/2 is 6/1 × 2/1 = 12, because flipping 1/2 gives a factor larger than 1. Dividing by a number less than 1 always makes the quotient grow.
level3.explanationEs: Las dos expresiones hacen preguntas distintas, y el volteo muestra por qué. 6 ÷ 2 es 6/1 × 1/2 = 3, porque voltear 2/1 da un factor menor que 1. 6 ÷ 1/2 es 6/1 × 2/1 = 12, porque voltear 1/2 da un factor mayor que 1. Dividir entre un número menor que 1 siempre hace crecer el cociente.
level3.promptEs: Dividir 6 entre 1/2 da 12, pero dividir 6 entre 2 da 3. ¿Cómo puede dividir entre un número más pequeño (1/2) dar una respuesta más grande que dividir entre un número más grande (2)? Explica con un ejemplo de la vida real.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer ambas: 6 ÷ 2 reparte 6 en 2 grupos iguales, pero 6 ÷ 1/2 cuenta cuántas piezas de medio tamaño caben en 6.
Escoge un objeto real —6 sándwiches repartidos entre 2 personas frente a 6 sándwiches cortados por la mitad— y describe las dos situaciones.
Empieza tu respuesta con la historia de repartir (6 en 2 grupos) y luego explica qué le hace al conteo cortar por la mitad.
